#!/bin/bash

#PBS -P CBBI1106
#PBS -N array_job
#PBS -l select=1:ncpus=24
#PBS -o /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.out
#PBS -e /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.err
#PBS -l walltime=1:00:00
#PBS -J 1-21:21
#PBS -q smp
#PBS -M belindalombard@sun.ac.za
#PBS -m be

sleep 4

#module add chpc/BIOMODULES R/4.1.0

# Add R module (includes appropriate openMPI and gcc modules)
module add chpc/R/3.5.1-gcc7.2.0

# make sure we're in the correct working directory.
cd /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/

make sbv

STEP=21
START=$PBS_ARRAY_INDEX
END=$(( $START+$STEP-1 ))

for i in $(eval echo "{$START..$END}")
do
	(echo "process $i started" && Rscript sbv/method_1_analysis/method_1_arrayjob.R $i && echo "process $i finished")& 
done

sleep 0.1 # For sequential output
echo "Waiting for processes to finish" 
wait $(jobs -p)
echo "All processes finished"
inputs.instruction:
Any command line flux submit option can be represented in a batch script:

#FLUX: --<arg>=<val>

As an example:

#FLUX: --cores=N

Here are the possible arguments from flux submit.
usage: flux submit [OPTIONS...] COMMAND [ARGS...]

enqueue a job

positional arguments:
  command                     Job command and arguments

options:
      --help=[TOPIC]          Show this help message or extended help for
                              TOPIC and exit
  -B, --bank=BANK             Submit a job to a specific named bank
  -q, --queue=NAME            Submit a job to a specific named queue
  -t, --time-limit=MIN|FSD    Time limit in minutes when no units provided,
                              otherwise in Flux standard duration, e.g. 30s,
                              2d, 1.5h
      --urgency=N             Set job urgency (0-31), hold=0, default=16,
                              expedite=31
      --job-name=NAME         Set an optional name for job to NAME
  -o, --setopt=OPT            Set shell option OPT. An optional value is
                              supported with OPT=VAL (default VAL=1) (multiple
                              use OK)
  -S, --setattr=ATTR          Set job attribute ATTR. An optional value is
                              supported with ATTR=VAL (default VAL=1). If ATTR
                              starts with ^, then VAL is a file containing
                              valid JSON which will be used as the value of
                              the attribute. (multiple use OK)
      --add-file=[NAME=]PATH  Add a file at PATH with optional NAME to
                              jobspec. The file will be extracted to
                              /NAME. If NAME is not specified, then
                              the basename of PATH will be used. If necessary,
                              permissions may be specified via NAME:PERMS.
                              (multiple use OK)
      --dependency=URI        Set an RFC 26 dependency URI for this job
      --requires=CONSTRAINT   Specify job constraints in RFC 35 syntax
      --begin-time=+FSD|TIME  Set minimum start time as offset in FSD (e.g.
                              +1h) or an absolute TIME (e.g. "3pm") for job
      --env=RULE              Control how environment variables are exported.
                              If RULE starts with '-' apply rest of RULE as a
                              remove filter (see --env-remove), if '^' then
                              read rules from a file (see --env-file).
                              Otherwise, set matching environment variables
                              from the current environment (--env=PATTERN) or
                              set a value explicitly (--env=VAR=VALUE). Rules
                              are applied in the order they are used on the
                              command line. (multiple use OK)
      --env-remove=PATTERN    Remove environment variables matching PATTERN.
                              If PATTERN starts with a '/', then it is matched
                              as a regular expression, otherwise PATTERN is a
                              shell glob expression. (multiple use OK)
      --env-file=FILE         Read a set of environment rules from FILE.
                              (multiple use OK)
      --rlimit=RULE           Control how soft resource limits are propagated
                              to the job. If RULE starts with a '-', then do
                              not propagate matching resource limits (e.g.
                              '-*' propagates nothing). Otherwise, propagate
                              the current limit or a specific value, e.g.
                              --rlimit=core or --rlimit=core=16. The option
                              may be used multiple times to build a reduced
                              set of propagated limits, e.g. --rlimit=-*,core
                              will only propagate RLIMIT_CORE.
      --input=FILENAME        Redirect job stdin from FILENAME, bypassing KVS
      --output=FILENAME       Redirect job stdout to FILENAME, bypassing KVS
      --error=FILENAME        Redirect job stderr to FILENAME, bypassing KVS
  -u, --unbuffered            Disable buffering of input and output
  -l, --label-io              Add rank labels to stdout, stderr lines
      --cwd=DIRECTORY         Set job working directory
      --flags=FLAGS           Set comma separated list of job submission
                              flags. Possible flags: debug, waitable,
                              novalidate
      --signal=[SIG][@TIME]   Schedule delivery of signal SIG at a defined
                              TIME before job expiration. Default SIG is
                              SIGUSR1, default TIME is 60s.
      --dry-run               Don't actually submit job, just emit jobspec
      --quiet                 Do not print jobid to stdout on submission
      --taskmap=URI           Select the scheme for mapping task ids to nodes
                              as a URI (i.e. SCHEME[:VALUE]). Value options
                              include block, cyclic, cyclic:N, or
                              manual:TASKMAP (default: block)
  -v, --verbose               Increase verbosity on stderr (multiple use OK)
      --cc=IDSET              Replicate job for each ID in IDSET.
                              (FLUX_JOB_CC=ID will be set for each job
                              submitted)
      --bcc=IDSET             Like --cc, but FLUX_JOB_CC is not set
      --wait-event=NAME       Wait for event NAME for all jobs after
                              submission
      --wait                  Wait for all jobs to complete after submission
                              (same as --wait-event=clean)
      --watch                 Watch all job output (implies --wait)
      --log=FILE              Print program log messages (e.g. submitted
                              jobid) to FILE instead of terminal
      --log-stderr=FILE       Separate stderr messages into FILE instead of
                              terminal or logfile destination
      --progress              Show progress of job submission or completion
                              (with --wait)
      --jps                   With --progress, show job throughput

Common resource options:
  -N, --nodes=N               Number of nodes to allocate
  -x, --exclusive             With -N, --nodes, allocate nodes exclusively

Per task options:
  The following options allow per-task specification of resources, and
  should not be combined with per-resource options.

  -n, --ntasks=N              Number of tasks to start
  -c, --cores-per-task=N      Number of cores to allocate per task
  -g, --gpus-per-task=N       Number of GPUs to allocate per task

Per resource options:
  The following options allow per-resource specification of tasks, and
  should not be used with per-task options above

      --cores=N               Request a total number of cores
      --tasks-per-node=N      Force number of tasks per node
      --tasks-per-core=N      Force number of tasks per core
      --gpus-per-node=N       Request a number of GPUs per node with --nodes

You MUST ignore accounts, partitions, projects, mail, banks, queues, and notifications.
You MUST omit these from issues and the translation if there is no obvious translation.
You MUST try to minimize issues.
You MUST ignore commented out directives.
You MUST not guess and only include directives you are certain about.
If you need to calculate --ntasks-per-socket, assume the machine has 16 cores per socket and use --tasks-per-core.
Flux models affinity with broker arguments. E.g, -o cpu-affinity=per-task, -o gpu-affinity=per-task

outputs.summary: The PBS job array script was converted to a Flux batch script. The directives for job name, resource requests, I/O redirection, and walltime were translated. The core logic change involves adapting the job array mechanism. The PBS `-J` directive and `PBS_ARRAY_INDEX` variable were replaced by the Flux `--cc` submission flag and `FLUX_JOB_CC` environment variable. The internal loop logic of the script, which processes multiple items per job array task, was preserved.
issues: MISSING: The PBS job array directive `-J 1-21:21` defines a job array with a specific step size. Flux does not support a step size in its job collection (`--cc`) directive. This behavior must be replicated by submitting the job with a specific range, e.g., `flux submit --cc=1,22,43,...` or by handling the step logic inside the script. The provided translation assumes the user will handle the stepping logic at submission time and sets the loop to process a single starting index from `FLUX_JOB_CC`.
outputs.implications: The job will not run as a stepped array out-of-the-box. The user must manually generate the correct sequence of starting indices for the `--cc` flag (e.g., 1, 22, 43, ...) to replicate the original PBS behavior. If submitted with `--cc=1-21`, the script will run 21 tasks, but they will process overlapping data ranges, leading to incorrect and redundant computations. The provided translation adjusts the internal loop to handle a single start index per task, but this relies on the user providing the correct stepped indices at submission.

#!/bin/bash

# The -P, -q, -M, and -m directives are ignored as per instructions.
#FLUX: --job-name=array_job
# The PBS select statement is translated to the following flux directives:
#FLUX: --nodes=1
#FLUX: --cores=24
#FLUX: --output=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.out
#FLUX: --error=/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.err
#FLUX: --time-limit=1h
# The PBS job array `-J 1-21:21` is not directly translatable. This script must be submitted
# with a manually stepped list of indices, e.g., `flux submit --cc=1,22,43,...`

sleep 4

#module add chpc/BIOMODULES R/4.1.0

# Add R module (includes appropriate openMPI and gcc modules)
module add chpc/R/3.5.1-gcc7.2.0

# make sure we're in the correct working directory.
cd /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/

make sbv

STEP=21
# The PBS_ARRAY_INDEX is replaced with FLUX_JOB_CC.
START=$FLUX_JOB_CC
END=$(( $START+$STEP-1 ))

for i in $(eval echo "{$START..$END}")
do
	(echo "process $i started" && Rscript sbv/method_1_analysis/method_1_arrayjob.R $i && echo "process $i finished")& 
done

sleep 0.1 # For sequential output
echo "Waiting for processes to finish" 
wait $(jobs -p)
echo "All processes finished"

### PERSONA
You are an autonomous sub-agent with expertise in transforming job specifications.

### CONSTRAINTS
- You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
- You MUST get the true job identifier.
- You MUST NOT touch or inspect other jobs.

- If there is a directive that does not translate, you MUST leave it out and add a comment about the performance implications of the omission.
- You MUST preserve as many options as possible from the original.
- If you have a tool available, you MUST use it to validate the conversion.
- If you do not have a tool available, you MUST provide a "reason" the script is valid.

### INSTRUCTIONS
1. Analyze the original script provided in the CONTEXT.
2. Write a new script that converts from pbs to flux.
3. Return the finished job specification in a JSON markdown code block with the key "jobspec".
4. Scrutinize your result and provide a list of "issues" one per item, in a "missing" return value.
  An issue might be:
    UNKNOWN_TO_ME: There is a parameter I am not familiar with that I cannot figure out (and provide detail)
    NO_ANALOGOUS: The from parameter has no analogous translation (and provide it)
    MISSING: You are not aware of any possible conversion (and details)
5. If you can predict the performance or other implications of the conversion, include them in "implications"
6. If the input script is not a workload manager batch file, you MUST return the JSON "jobspec" value as "noop".

- When you make each decision (response or tool call) you MUST return a JSON object with your reason/thinking:
- When you are finished, you MUST return ONE final JSON object:
 {"action": "stop", "summary": "...", "issues": ["NO_ANALOGOUS: the parameter..."], "implications": "...", "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash ...", "reason": "..."}

Convert the provided job specification from pbs to flux. The desired output format is a 'batch' script.
